results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Source opens: "By the time you're done with Edinburgh art festival you'll have uncovered so many hidden stories you'll feel like Columbo."
results.REASON: Positive meta-source claim about what the reviewer writes; the anchor is the source's own opening sentence, quoted essentially verbatim.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Source: "There are curated displays, satellite exhibitions, performances, off-site projects, and it's impossible to figure out how any of it fits together."
results.REASON: Asserts what the reviewer's account holds; the source states exactly that in its own voice.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Source: "You can't walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you've never heard of."
results.REASON: Positive claim about what the review says; verbatim anchor present.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Source: "You can't walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you've never heard of."

results.NEGATIVE_CLAIM: The review does not place Sandra George and Frank Walter above the rest of the festival.
results.SCOPE: Would require the whole review: ranking, preference and elevation can be carried implicitly by tone, space, ordering and evaluative adjectives anywhere in the text.
results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: No explicit statement of non-ranking exists in the source, and no finite textual scope can be stated whose exhaustion would demonstrate the absence of a ranking. The only available reasoning is 'no explicit ranking sentence was found', which is not a proof type. In fact the source contains distributed evaluative preference ('worth telling', 'deserves to be seen far outside the city's confines', 'it's all eclipsed by his weird little paintings', 'don't do a lot for me', 'none of them good'), which is exactly the implicit, tone-carried ranking that cannot be scanned away.
results.WHY_SCOPE_IS_COMPLETE: Scope cannot be bounded: the property (relative elevation of two artists) is semantic and distributable across the entire review, so no statable scope is exhaustible.
results.REASON: Negative claim about a semantic property of the whole source, extraction anchor empty, and its only possible support is failure to find contrary text. Neither EXPLICIT nor BOUNDED_ABSENCE survives.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Source, in the body of the review: "If contemporary artists and institutions want to tell hidden stories, I think they have a duty - to viewers and to their subjects - to tell them clearly." It falls in the middle stretch of the piece (13th of 19 paragraphs), neither in the opening framing nor in the closing verdict.
results.REASON: Positional claim about where something appears in the source, which is in scope and here textually checkable. The demand exists and sits in the body; 'midway' is approximate but not misdescriptive.

results.REASON: Read as a claim about the source's diction rather than about the festival, it is the article's analytic framing ('characteristic verb') of a recurrence that is real in the source. It asserts no new factual state about the source's behaviour.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Frequency is directly countable in the source: 'uncovered so many hidden stories' (para 1), 'undiscovered archives' (para 1), 'only discovered after her death in 2013' (para 4), 'Another largely undiscovered artist' (para 17), 'previously undiscovered marginalised artist' (para 18), 'undiscovered narratives' (para 19).
results.REASON: Positive claim about how often the source reaches for a word family; six occurrences across the piece are present, so the repetition claim is licensed by the text itself.

Reasonable analysis of source-grounded material rather than a licensed new fact about his conduct.

results.REASON: The review does add this point about Hasegawa. Note a minor quantifier drift: the source says 'Most of' his work, the proposition drops the qualifier. The attribution itself is licensed.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Every occurrence of the word family in the source attaches to a finder or viewer: the visitor who has 'uncovered so many hidden stories', the archives that are 'undiscovered' to us, George 'only discovered after her death', the gallery-goer who has 'never heard of this previously undiscovered marginalised artist'.
results.REASON: Extraction anchor empty, but this is analysis of the source's own usage pattern rather than a new factual assertion about the source's behaviour.

results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: Analysis of the same usage pattern: the source consistently uses the word at the point at which work becomes visible to someone who did not know of it.
results.REASON: Semantic gloss on the word as the source deploys it; asserts no new factual state about the source.

results.NEGATIVE_CLAIM: The word 'discovery' (and its family), as the review uses it, does not and cannot describe the span of years in which the work went unshown during its maker's lifetime.
results.SCOPE: The finite, enumerable set of occurrences of the discovery word family in the source: 'uncovered so many hidden stories', 'undiscovered archives', 'only discovered after her death in 2013', 'Another largely undiscovered artist', 'previously undiscovered marginalised artist', 'undiscovered narratives'. The property is textual (what each occurrence attaches to), not tonal or distributable.
results.EVIDENCE_OR_METHOD: All six occurrences were enumerated and each attaches to the moment or fact of becoming visible to a finder, never to the interval of non-showing. Positively corroborating: where the source does name that interval it uses entirely different words - 'she never showed her work publicly in her lifetime', 'died having never shown any of the thousands of paintings and drawings he amassed over his lifetime', 'stayed unpublished and unseen in his lifetime' - so the source itself lexically separates the two spans. The modal 'cannot' is a claim about the word's sense (discovery names the finder's event), not a claim resting on failure to find text.
results.WHY_SCOPE_IS_COMPLETE: The scope is every token of the discovery word family in the source text; the source is short and fully given, the token set is finite and was listed exhaustively, and the property checked (what the token predicates of) is decidable per token. Nothing outside that token set could bear on what the word describes.
results.REASON: A negative source claim that survives: bounded, statable, exhausted, and additionally corroborated by the source using distinct vocabulary for the unshown years. Not rejected merely for being negative.
